comments.body:
Implementation done in worktree ../reopen-parent-cascade (branch reopen-parent-cascade), TDD RED-first.

RED: added 7 reopen cases to tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py; 4 failed against unpatched code (closed parent stayed closed on reopen; multi-level chain not cascaded; raced parent DID NOT RAISE; CLI parity), 3 passed trivially (the no-op parent cases).

GREEN: generalized the existing cascade seam instead of adding a second one.
- _resolve_open_parent -> new _resolve_parent_in_status(tracker, ticket_id, status); _resolve_open_parent is now its 'open' specialization, so claim.py is untouched.
- _cascade_open_parent -> _cascade_parent_first, driven by a module-level _CASCADING_EDGES table mapping the child's (current, target) edge to the parent status eligible on it: ('open','in_progress') -> 'open' (unchanged) and ('closed','open') -> 'closed' (the fix). The parent moves along the SAME edge, ahead of the child, under the existing _cascade_seen cycle guard and the existing fail-fast error wrapping (message names the parent; ConcurrencyMismatch identity/exit 10 preserved).
- Stale symbol references updated per the plan-review advisory: the transition.py call-site comment and the transition_close.py module docstring.
- reopen docstring (_lib_writes.py) and docs/concurrency.md I4a updated; I4a now tables both cascading edges and explains why the close-time open-children guard's asymmetry made this edge necessary.

Semantics note on AC1's word 'atomic': delivered as the documented claim/transition cascade shape it is asked to mirror - one user-visible invocation, sequential and fail-fast, NOT transactional (no rollback if the parent succeeds and the child then fails). That is docs/concurrency.md I4a's existing contract; making reopen transactional would have been a different, larger change to the shared seam.

Scope note: transition_close.py (one-word docstring cross-reference) was added to file_impact after the fact.

Gates locally green: make lint (incl. complexity ratchet new=0 increased=0 stale=0), make typecheck, and tests/interfaces/lifecycle + tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py = 513 passed. transition.py is 741 LOC, under the 800 cap.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar reopen <child>` moves a closed ticket to open but does NOT cascade to its
still-closed parent(s). `reopen` is a thin delegation to
`transition(ticket_id, "closed", "open")` (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:430`, and the CLI
`reopen_cli` at `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:689`), and the parent-first cascade in
`transition_compute` fires only on the `open -> in_progress` edge
(`_cascade_open_parent`, `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:387`). Combined with the
close-time open-children guard (which only blocks CLOSING a parent that has open
children), this lets the store reach an invalid state: a CLOSED parent with an
OPEN/in_progress child.

Observed while closing epic e215-ab23-ed6a-4791: after the epic returned to `closed`,
reopening child stories aabf-d89e-d05a-45c4 (S7) and 075b-1479-dcb7-40ab (S7.3) left the
epic `closed` while the children were `in_progress`.

## Approach
Generalize the existing cascade seam rather than adding a second parallel one, so both
edges keep one implementation, one error shape, and one cycle guard.

1. Add `_resolve_parent_in_status(tracker, ticket_id, status)` next to the existing
   `_resolve_open_parent` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:93`), which today hardcodes
   the `"open"` comparison. `_resolve_open_parent` becomes a one-line delegation to it, so
   its other caller (`src/rebar/_commands/claim.py:190,193,215`) needs no edit.
2. Replace `_cascade_open_parent` with an edge-table-driven `_cascade_parent_first`: a
   module-level mapping from `(current_status, target_status)` to the parent status that
   is eligible to cascade — `("open", "in_progress") -> "open"` (today's behavior,
   unchanged) and `("closed", "open") -> "closed"` (the fix). The parent is transitioned
   on the SAME edge as the child before the child moves, recursing up the chain under the
   existing `_cascade_seen` cycle guard, with the existing fail-fast error wrapping that
   names the parent and preserves `ConcurrencyMismatch` (exit 10).
3. Update the `reopen` docstring (`src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:430`) and `docs/concurrency.md`
   §I4a, whose line 115 currently states that `close`/`reopen`/`blocked` never cascade.

Why this approach fits: the invariant being restored ("a parent is never more closed than
its children") is symmetric with the one `open -> in_progress` already enforces, and the
existing helper already carries the fail-fast, exit-code-preserving, cycle-guarded
semantics this edge needs. A separate copy of that logic would be a second place to drift.

Cascade semantics deliberately MIRROR the documented `claim`/`transition` cascade
(`docs/concurrency.md` §I4a): a single user-visible invocation that is sequential and
fail-fast, NOT transactional — if the parent op fails the child op is not attempted and
the parent failure's exit code is preserved; if the parent succeeds and the child then
fails there is no rollback. Only the `closed -> open` edge is added; `* -> closed` keeps
its existing non-cascading behavior and its open-children guard, and a parent that is
`in_progress`/`blocked`/`open`/absent is not cascaded.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` — add `_resolve_parent_in_status`, reduce
  `_resolve_open_parent` to a delegation, replace `_cascade_open_parent` with the
  edge-table-driven `_cascade_parent_first`, update its call site in `transition_compute`
  (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:415`).
- `src/rebar/_lib_writes.py` — document the reopen cascade on `reopen`.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py` — add the reopen
  cascade cases alongside the existing claim/transition cascade cases.
- `docs/concurrency.md` — update §I4a to describe both cascading edges.

Assume the existing fail-fast/no-rollback contract is correct and is not being revisited
here; this ticket only widens which edges it applies to.

## Testing
Held-out tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py`,
using the existing `rebar_repo` fixture and `_status()` helper already in that file:
- Happy path: reopen a closed child under a closed parent -> both are `open`.
- No-op path: reopen a closed child whose parent is already `open` (and, separately,
  already `in_progress`) -> the parent's status is untouched.
- Multi-level: a closed grand/parent/child chain, reopen the leaf -> all three are `open`.
- Failure/edge path: monkeypatch `txn.transition_core` to raise `ConcurrencyMismatch` for
  the parent -> `rebar.reopen(child)` raises `ConcurrencyError` with `returncode == 10`,
  the error names the parent, and the child is still `closed` (no partial cascade).
- Regression: closing a child still does NOT cascade to its parent
  (`test_close_does_not_cascade_to_parent` must keep passing).
Run with `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_claim_transition_parent_cascade.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Reopening a child whose parent is closed also reopens the parent, transitively to
      the root, in a single invocation that mirrors the claim/transition parent-first
      cascade (parent moved before the child; sequential and fail-fast, not
      transactional). Checked by the happy-path and multi-level tests above asserting
      every ancestor's status is `open` after one `rebar.reopen(leaf)` call.
- [ ] The parent/child status invariant holds after a reopen: no closed parent is left
      with a non-closed child. Checked by asserting the parent's status is `open` (not
      `closed`) in the happy-path and multi-level tests, and by the no-op tests asserting
      an already-`open`/`in_progress` parent is not disturbed.
- [ ] Held-out tests cover all four cases in `## Testing`: reopen under a closed parent,
      reopen under an already-open parent, a multi-level chain, and a raced parent
      surfacing `ConcurrencyError`/exit 10 with the child left `closed`. Checked by the
      named test file passing under pytest.
- [ ] `docs/concurrency.md` §I4a describes the reopen (`closed -> open`) parent-first
      cascade alongside the existing `open -> in_progress` cascade, and no longer states
      that `reopen` never cascades. Checked by reading the updated §I4a.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass, including the shrink-only complexity ratchet
      (`python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no `new` or
      `increased` entries).
